meta.name: Generate quality-checked YouTube thumbnails with OpenAI and Google Drive

name: AI YouTube Thumbnail Generator - Quality Checked

parameters.content:
## AI YouTube Thumbnail Generator - Quality Checked

### How it works

This workflow generates YouTube thumbnail images from a form submission by collecting character references and example thumbnail designs from Google Drive. It uses OpenAI to analyze those inputs, builds structured image prompts with an AI Agent, generates images through the OpenAI Images API, uploads or stores the results, and checks image quality with another AI review step. Approved images are logged to Google Sheets, while failed quality checks are retried until a limit is reached and then routed for manual review.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger fields so the workflow receives the required thumbnail request details and any folder or file identifiers it needs.
- Connect Google Drive credentials and set the correct folders/files for character references, thumbnail examples, and generated image storage.
- Configure OpenAI credentials for the analysis nodes, AI Agent chat model, and the image generation HTTP request/API key.
- Set up Cloudinary credentials or replace the Cloudinary upload URL and parameters in the image URL step with your own image hosting configuration.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheet/sheet where approved thumbnail results should be recorded.
- Review the retry counter code and the retry-limit condition so they match your acceptable number of regeneration attempts.

### Customization

You can adjust the AI Agent instructions, structured output schema, image generation parameters, quality-check criteria, destination folders, and retry limit to match a specific thumbnail style or production process.

## Receive thumbnail request

Starts the workflow when a user submits the form and fans out into the character-reference and thumbnail-example collection paths.

## Fetch character files

Retrieves the character reference files from Google Drive and downloads them for AI analysis.

## Fetch example thumbnails

Retrieves example thumbnail design files from Google Drive and downloads them for design analysis.

## Analyze character references

Uses OpenAI to interpret the downloaded character images and aggregates the character descriptions for prompt building.

## Analyze thumbnail style

Uses OpenAI to analyze the example thumbnail designs and aggregates the extracted design guidance.

## Build generation prompts

Combines the character and design analysis, then uses an AI Agent with a chat model and structured parser to produce usable image-generation prompts.

## Generate image file

Processes prompts one at a time, resets the per-item retry counter, calls the image generation API, and converts the generated image data into a file.

## Store image outputs

Uploads or stores the generated image through Cloudinary and Google Drive, merges the resulting metadata, and splits it into items for downstream quality review.

## Review and log approval

Evaluates the generated thumbnail quality with OpenAI, branches on the result, and records approved images in Google Sheets before returning to the batch loop.

## Handle failed quality

Counts failed quality-check attempts, decides whether another generation retry is allowed, and sends exhausted items to manual review before continuing the loop.

parameters.formDescription: Generate Premium YouTube Thumbnails in seconds.

parameters.text:
=You are a professional YouTube thumbnail strategist. Analyze the uploaded creator image with the goal of helping another AI agent generate a personalized thumbnail around this person for {{ $('When Form Submitted').first().json['Video Title'] }}

Do not describe what the person does or what the video is about. Focus only on the visual characteristics of the person and the photo, to create a design blueprint for thumbnails featuring them.

** Identify the following **

- Face Positioning & Angle: Is the subject facing forward, looking to the side, angled? How much of the face is visible?

- Facial Expression & Emotion: What emotion is conveyed — surprise, curiosity, confidence, joy, etc.? How strong is the expression?

- Lighting Style: Describe lighting (natural, harsh, studio-lit, moody, bright) and its direction (front-lit, back-lit, side-lit).

- Pose & Body Language: Is the subject pointing, gesturing, using props? How dynamic or static is the pose?

- Clothing/Accessories: Any standout colors or elements that should be preserved for brand consistency?

- Background: What type of background is there? Plain, blurred, colored, environmental? Can it be removed or replaced?

- Color Palette & Skin Tone: Note any dominant tones (warm, cool, neutral) that should be preserved in design.

Your output should form a visual personality profile of the creator — the kind of emotional tone, framing, and style that best represents them in thumbnails.

Output should be generic and reusable. Avoid product/topic references. Focus on helping another agent design brand-consistent, emotionally resonant creator images to be used in YouTube Thumbnail creation later.

=You are a professional YouTube thumbnail designer tasked with reverse-engineering the success of multiple thumbnails.

Analyze the uploaded images holistically — without focusing on the specific product, brand, or content shown. Instead, break down the visual strategies and design principles that make these thumbnails effective.

** For each image, extract **

- Visual Style Summary: What stands out first? Is the design loud, minimal, energetic, dramatic, etc.?

- Subject Framing & Emotion: Describe the positioning of the main subject (if present), including body language, facial expression, and emotional tone conveyed.

- Typography and Text Layout: Where is the text placed? What style is it in (bold, shadowed, uppercase, etc.)? How does it contribute to attention capture?

- Color Palette & Contrast: What are the dominant colors? How is contrast used to create visual separation and draw attention?

- Background Treatment: Is the background blurred, flat, colorful, gradient, or abstract? Does it enhance or compete with the subject?

- Visual Hierarchy: Which elements pull focus first, second, and third? How is balance achieved?

- Thumbnail Style Type (optional): Is it close-up face-focused, action shot, object-based, diagrammatic, meme-style, etc.?

After analyzing all images, provide a synthesized overview of recurring design patterns or style themes across them. These insights should help us build versatile thumbnail templates that can be reused for different topics in future automations.

Do not describe the product or content in the image. Keep outputs generic and focused on style patterns, layout structures, and attention-driving design tactics.

=You are reviewing a generated YouTube thumbnail for quality.

Evaluate the image using these criteria:

The image is high quality, sharp, and visually polished.
Important text is clearly visible, readable, and not cropped or truncated.
The main character should reasonably match one of these creator descriptions:
{{ $('Aggregate Characters Data').item.json['Images Description'] }}
The thumbnail should contain a clear visual hierarchy with a main character or primary subject, readable thumbnail text, and a supporting visual element such as an icon, object, graphic, effect, or relevant visual cue.
A tool or software icon is required only when a specific tool, app, platform, or software product is mentioned in the video title.
If the video title does not mention a tool or software product, do not reject the thumbnail because a tool icon is missing.
The thumbnail should have strong contrast, good composition, and clear focal points.
There should be no obvious AI-generation defects, malformed objects, broken text, duplicated elements, or distracting artifacts.
The thumbnail should look suitable for professional YouTube use.

If the thumbnail passes the important quality requirements, respond exactly with:

yes

If the thumbnail has a significant quality problem, respond exactly with:

no

Return only yes or no. Do not provide explanations. Do not add punctuation.

options.systemMessage:
=** Purpose **
Generate high-impact YouTube thumbnail prompts using the provided video title, creators images, and a proven high-converting visual style. Each prompt must guide an AI system to create a visually compelling thumbnail that boosts click-through rates and aligns with the creator’s visual brand.

** How It Works **
You will receive information about multiple images, both for character descriptions and thumbnails descriptions. Based on this information, choose the most proper data to create a high-quality thumbnail based on this video title: "{{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Video Title'] }}" Then follow this process:

** Analyze & Remix the Style **

- Treat the visual style template as the base structure.
- Blend this with the video title, creator image, and emotional tone from the original design.
- Maintain consistency with the creator’s personality and image tone (e.g., face angle, expression, clothing, colors).

** Build a Prompt for Thumbnail Generation **

- Highlight the video title (use: {{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Video Title'] }} as placeholder).
- Integrate the creator image naturally and prominently (use: {{ $('Aggregate Thumbnails Data').first().json['Thumbnails Description'] }} as placeholder).
- Maintain the visual and emotional tone of the template (use: {{ $('Aggregate Characters Data').item.json['Images Description'] }} as reference).
- Add 3D generated icon element for the tool mentioned in {{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Video Title'] }} next to the text.

For Example:
1.
title: NEW Deepseek Update!
result: Add deepseek icon

2.
title: n8n Workflow
result: Add n8n icon

If there is no tool name in the title, don't create it
Ensure the final result communicates clarity, trust, and visual impact.

** Output Rules **

- Output exactly 1 thumbnail generation prompt. Do not output more or fewer.
- Do not explain the steps or the process.
- Use placeholders like {{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Video Title'] }} so it works across workflows.
- Keep the formatting plain (no markdown, no styling).
- Never mention product names or actual user data — just use placeholders.
- Return exactly one distinct prompt object.
Return only the single structured prompt object required by the connected Structured Output Parser.

** Sample Use Case **
You are given:

- {{ $('Aggregate Characters Data').item.json['Images Description'] }} as visual style input
- {{ $('Aggregate Thumbnails Data').first().json['Thumbnails Description'] }} as transparent hero image
- {{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json['Video Title'] }} as the main title to feature

Your task is to return one static thumbnail prompt that blends these elements into a unique but consistent, scroll-stopping thumbnail design.
- Do not copy a reference thumbnail exactly. Borrow only general layout/style principles and create an original composition.
- Only use a real person's likeness when the user owns the image or has permission to use it.
